title: beads-bootstrap.sh rm -rf's local engine gated only on a local '0' count — verify recoverability BEFORE deleting
description:
scripts/beads-bootstrap.sh runs automatically every SessionStart (via install-bd.sh). When 'bd stats' reports 0 issues it executes 'rm -rf .beads/embeddeddolt .beads/dolt' and THEN tries 'bd bootstrap' to pull from origin. It never verifies origin actually carries refs/dolt/data before deleting. Combined with Bench-h4f (origin often has no ref), this is a latent data-loss hazard: 'delete, then hope'. (Note: it removes only the engine subdirs and guards on '[ -d .beads ]', so it cannot delete .beads/ wholesale — scope the fix to the engine-clear path.)

Acceptance criteria:
- Invert the order: prove a recovery source exists (origin refs/dolt/data reachable, OR a non-empty committed .beads/issues.jsonl) BEFORE removing any engine dir.
- If neither source exists, refuse to clear and log a loud warning; leave the (possibly cold) local engine intact.
- Red test: with bd stats=0 and origin carrying NO refs/dolt/data and no committed issues.jsonl, the script must NOT rm the engine dirs and must exit non-destructively.

title: bench:init never establishes refs/dolt/data on origin — local-only boards have no rehydrate source
description:
Bench's entire rehydrate model assumes 'reachable Dolt history lives on git origin under refs/dolt/data' (stated in scripts/beads-bootstrap.sh). But nothing in commands/init.md, templates/CLAUDE.bench.md, or any script ever runs 'bd dolt remote add' or 'bd dolt push'. The ONLY code that creates refs/dolt/data is scripts/beads-cloud-push.sh, which is web-only (gated on CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true). Net: a local-only Bench user never gets a portable rehydrate source, so every cold-board bootstrap is an unrecoverable no-op.

Acceptance criteria:
- bench:init Step 2 configures a Dolt remote (origin) and performs an initial 'bd dolt push' so refs/dolt/data exists from day one.
- init verifies .beads/issues.jsonl is COMMITTED (not merely staged).
- A non-web local SessionEnd path keeps origin's refs/dolt/data current (generalize beads-cloud-push.sh or add a local equivalent).
- Red test: a fresh 'bench:init' in a repo with an origin results in 'git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/*' returning a ref.
close_reason: bench:init patch merged in PR #5 (establishes refs/dolt/data on origin + verifies committed jsonl). Dogfooded on this repo: refs/dolt/data now present on origin (34a07b2).

comments.author: research-session

title: Local board reversion: .beads git hooks auto-import stale committed issues.jsonl on worktree-add/merge
description: Observed live 2026-07-03: 'bd close Bench-uba' succeeded, but after the orchestrator created a scratch integration worktree (git worktree add -> post-checkout hook) and merged 4 feature branches in it (git merge x4 -> post-merge hook), Bench-uba reverted to its Jun-29 OPEN row (Updated timestamp regressed; the close event vanished). Rows created after the trigger survived (import doesn't delete unknown rows); rows whose committed-jsonl snapshot was stale got clobbered. This is the LOCAL twin of the cloud reversion bug fixed by beads-cloud-push.sh: bd's own .beads/hooks (post-checkout/post-merge run 'bd hooks run <name>') treat the committed .beads/issues.jsonl as an import source, and every feature branch/worktree carries a stale snapshot. The bench-orchestrator SKILL.md footgun section warns against HAND-merging jsonl but not about bd's own hooks re-importing on checkout/merge. ## Repro hypothesis 1. Close a bead. 2. git worktree add a branch whose committed issues.jsonl predates the close (or merge such a branch). 3. bd show the bead -> reverted. ## Acceptance criteria - Confirmed repro + root cause (which hook, what import semantics in bd 1.0.4). - Mitigation shipped: orchestrator SKILL.md integration steps use hook-suppressed merges (git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null merge) followed by bd export + commit from the main tree; and/or beads-health-check gains a detection check (row Updated-timestamp regression vs export-state). - Consider upstream issue to gastownhall/beads.

title: doctor/health-check: add RED invariant — destructive bootstrap enabled + no recoverable source
description:
skills/beads-health-check/SKILL.md reads and compares refs/dolt/data and can push it, but nothing asserts the dangerous combination that causes loss: destructive bootstrap path enabled AND no recoverable source (no origin refs/dolt/data AND no non-empty committed .beads/issues.jsonl) = RED. Also steer Bench projects OFF the global/shared Dolt engine toward a repo-local engine.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Create a beads board whose only copy is the local engine (no 'bd dolt push', issues.jsonl not committed).
2. Run a Bench health-check / doctor. Before this fix it reports no problem.
3. A cold-start (or misresolved empty DB) then clears the engine with nothing to rehydrate from → board lost.

## Acceptance Criteria
- beads-health-check emits a RED finding when bootstrap-clear is reachable and no recovery source exists.
- doctor reports global/shared-engine usage as a warning with the repo-local remediation.
close_reason: Re-close: original close today (2026-07-03) was reverted to the stale Jun-29 row by a jsonl auto-import (see the reversion bug bead filed alongside this). Work verified in-tree: RED invariant present in doctor.md + beads-health-check SKILL.md.

(4) Add delegation guidance (when work fans out across independent items, delegate to Workers rather than iterating serially). (5) Add autonomy snippet: proceed on routine routing decisions (next gate, model choice, worktree naming) and note them; ask only for scope changes, destructive actions, or bounce-cap escalation. title: Mechanical bounce-cap: ROUND counters in qa/reviewer handoffs + reviewer coverage sentence

title: PreToolUse guard hooks: deny TodoWrite/TaskCreate, require --actor on bd writes, block checkout/switch/restore in shared tree
description: Opus 4.8 review firm-up (mechanical enforcement of prompt conventions). Ship in plugins/bench/: (1) scripts/guard-task-tools.sh - PreToolUse hook matching TodoWrite/TaskCreate/TaskUpdate tool calls: deny (exit 2) with stderr 'this project tracks work in beads - use bd create/update/close'. (2) scripts/guard-bd-actor.sh - PreToolUse on Bash: if the command runs a bd WRITE verb (create|update|close|comment|dep|delete|reopen) without --actor=, deny with a reminder that --actor is required inline on every bd write. Read-only bd commands pass. (3) scripts/guard-checkout.sh - PreToolUse on Bash: deny git checkout/switch/restore when CWD resolves to the MAIN worktree (git rev-parse --git-dir == --git-common-dir) AND .claude/worktrees has entries; allow inside linked worktrees; allow with BENCH_ALLOW_CHECKOUT=1 escape hatch. Wire all three into hooks/hooks.json under PreToolUse with correct matchers (check Claude Code hooks schema: PreToolUse receives tool name + input JSON on stdin; deny = exit 2 with message on stderr). ## Acceptance criteria (red-test list) - bats tests: TodoWrite denied with bd message; 'bd close X' without --actor denied, with --actor passes, 'bd list' passes; git checkout denied in main tree with worktrees present, allowed in linked worktree, allowed with escape hatch. - hooks.json validates (claude plugin validate --strict). - Guards are fast (no network, no bd invocation) and NEVER deny anything but their exact targets. ## Out of scope - Editing agent prompt files or templates (separate beads).

title: install-bd.sh: setsid absent on stock macOS - detached install silently no-ops
description: Found during install-bd hardening sandbox testing: setsid is not on stock macOS PATH (util-linux only), so the 'setsid nohup bash -c ... &' detached block never runs on most Macs - bd simply never installs via the background path. title: worktree-reap: CURRENT_TREE guard ineffective when invoked with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR set
description: Pre-existing latent bug (predates chore/consistency-sweep; identical on main). worktree-reap.sh does 'cd "$ROOT"' (=CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR) before computing CURRENT_TREE via 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel', so CURRENT_TREE always resolves to the MAIN tree, not the tree the caller was standing in. Effect: if the reaper is run from *inside* a worktree whose branch is merged (or HEAD unreachable), the [ "$wt_path" = "$CURRENT_TREE" ] guard never matches and the live tree is reaped out from under the caller. Not reachable on the wired SessionStart path (cwd = project root, so MAIN_TREE guard covers it), which is why it's low priority. The consistency-sweep case-widening ('$WT_DIR'/* instead of agent-*/wf_*) broadens the off-path blast radius of this bug (any-named tree now reapable-from-inside, not just agent-/wf_), motivating a fix. Repro: run reaper with cwd inside .claude/worktrees/<merged-tree> and CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<project root> -> the tree is removed. Fix: capture CURRENT_TREE from the caller's cwd before 'cd "$ROOT"', or resolve it via $PWD's git-common-dir, and keep the MAIN_TREE guard as a second line of defense. Surfaced during review of Bench-z0v.
